conceptBreakdown.heading: 6. Pointwise Operations & Composite Functions
conceptBreakdown.title: 6. Pointwise Operations & Composite Functions

summaryBox.title: Composition Domain
summaryBox.takeaway: Dom(g ∘ f) = {x ∈ Dom(f) | f(x) ∈ Dom(g)}. Never assume Dom(g ∘ f) equals Dom(f).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
COMPOSITION MAPPING FLOW
                        
          x ──[ f ]──► f(x) ──[ g ]──► g(f(x))
         (Domain A)    (Codomain B)    (Codomain C)
         └─────────────── g ∘ f ────────────────┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
Let $f: D_1 \to \mathbb{R}$ and $g: D_2 \to \mathbb{R}$.

1. **Sum & Difference**: $(f \pm g)(x) = f(x) \pm g(x)$, with domain $D_1 \cap D_2$.
2. **Product**: $(f \cdot g)(x) = f(x) \cdot g(x)$, with domain $D_1 \cap D_2$.
3. **Quotient**: $(f/g)(x) = f(x)/g(x)$, with domain $(D_1 \cap D_2) \setminus \{x \mid g(x) = 0\}$.

### Composite Functions ($g \circ f$)
Let $f: A \to B$ and $g: B \to C$. The **Composite Function** $g \circ f: A \to C$ is defined by:
$$\mathbf{(g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x))}$$

$$\mathbf{\text{Dom}(g \circ f) = \{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid x \in \text{Dom}(f) \land f(x) \in \text{Dom}(g)\}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 Piecewise Composition Algorithm
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Piecewise Composition Algorithm
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PIECEWISE COMPOSITION ALGORITHM
                       
   Let f(x) and g(x) be defined piecewise over split sub-domains.
   To construct g(f(x)):
   1. Substitute f(x) into g(y) wherever variable y appears.
   2. Restrict each branch using the compound condition: x ∈ Dom(f) ∧ f(x) ∈ Sub-domain of g.
conceptBreakdown.content:
To construct $g(f(x))$ when $f$ and $g$ are defined piecewise:
1. Substitute $f(x)$ into each formula branch of $g(y)$.
2. Enforce the two simultaneous domain restrictions: $x$ must lie in the branch domain of $f(x)$, and the resulting $f(x)$ must fall inside the branch condition for $g(y)$.
